title: Alexander Hamilton: Most Influential American?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore Alexander Hamilton's life and legacy, prompted by the Broadway musical Hamilton. They cover his disputed birth and orphaned youth in the Caribbean, his work at Beekman and Kruger mercantile, his education at King's College, his Revolutionary War service as Washington's aide and at Yorktown, his push for a strong central government, the Federalist Papers, his role as first Treasury Secretary (assumption, national bank, tariffs, the Dinner Table Compromise), the rivalry with Jefferson and Adams, the 1800 election tie, the duel with Aaron Burr, the Maria Reynolds affair and extortion scandal, and his lasting legacy. The episode ends with a listener mail shout-out to Jeff Beverage and a sign-off.
topics: First Bank of the United States

segments.title: Intro and the Hamilton musical
segments.summary: Hosts open with banter about the Broadway show Hamilton and why Hamilton is finally getting recognition as one of the most influential Americans.

segments.title: Hamilton's childhood and orphanhood
segments.summary: Discussion of Hamilton's disputed birth date and Caribbean origins, his Scottish merchant father who left the family, his mother's death, and his cousin's suicide. He was left to his own devices.

segments.title: Working at Beekman and Kruger and going to King's College
segments.summary: Hamilton at about fourteen ran a trading firm on St. Croix, wrote newspaper pieces and poetry, and was sent with a fund to New York, where he attended King's College.

segments.title: Political pamphlets and early revolutionary views
segments.summary: Hamilton wrote influential political pamphlets against British rule, favoring a loose colonial confederation, and as a youth wrote that he hoped for war to prove himself. The hosts also note he was a consistent abolitionist.

segments.title: Revolutionary War and service as Washington's aide
segments.summary: Hamilton captained an artillery unit in the Continental Army, impressed George Washington, and became his aide-de-camp, writing much of his correspondence. He later fought at Yorktown and pushed to get into battle.

segments.title: Articles of Confederation and the Constitutional Convention
segments.summary: After the war the states were in bad shape under the Articles of Confederation. Hamilton, a New York delegate, helped draft a new Constitution, though he was often absent from the debates.

segments.title: The Federalist Papers
segments.summary: Hamilton, John Jay and James Madison wrote the Federalist Papers to argue for ratification. The papers were later cited heavily by the Supreme Court.

segments.title: Treasury Secretary and the financial plan
segments.summary: As Washington's first Treasury Secretary, Hamilton tackled war debts and proposed tariffs, a central bank, infrastructure investment, and assumption of state debts. The Dinner Table Compromise moved the capital to the South in exchange for assumption. The hosts discuss his rivalry with Jefferson and the origins of the two-party system.

segments.title: Adams rivalry, 1800 election, and the Burr duel
segments.summary: Hamilton clashed with John Adams, whose publication of the Adams-related papers contributed to a tie in the 1800 election between Jefferson and Burr, decided by Congress. Hamilton opposed Burr and later was killed in a duel with him at Weehawken, where his son Philip had died in a duel three years earlier.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before the duel discussion.

segments.title: Maria Reynolds affair and legacy
segments.summary: Hamilton's affair with Maria Reynolds, the extortion by her husband James Reynolds, and Hamilton's public confession to protect his integrity. His reputation was damaged. After his death, critics like Adams, Jefferson and Madison attacked him. The hosts discuss his modern legacy, including the Stock Exchange, Bank of New York, New York Post, and the Grange.

segments.title: Listener mail: shout-out to Jeff Beverage
segments.summary: A listener thanks friend Jeff Beverage for taking in his pet turtle after a house fire, and the hosts give him a shout-out. Social media and contact information are read.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts sign off and direct listeners to the website and social media.
